proposals.before: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.
proposals.after: I have lived in your country for a long time, and I am loath to kill you [following the Tongjian variant; the extant Jinshu wording reads “I regret not killing you” and is judged probably corrupt in the Jinshu Jiaozhu; see the textual note in the literal translation].
proposals.sourceReason: Explicitly mark the Tongjian variant used for loath to kill you and preserve the contrary extant Jinshu reading plus the critical judgment. The complete independently approved literal note supplies both divergent witnesses. This avoids an unmarked emendation in the idiomatic field without altering Chinese.

units.zh: 及遼奔走，翰又北投宇文歸。
units.literal: When Liao fled in defeat, Han again north threw himself to Yuwen Gui.
units.en: When Duan Liao fled in defeat, Han again went north to Yuwen Gui.

units.zh: 既而逃，歸乃遣勁騎百餘追之。
units.literal: Having then fled, Gui thereupon sent fierce cavalry over a hundred to pursue him.
units.en: Han then fled, and Gui sent over a hundred picked cavalry to pursue him.

units.zh: 翰遙謂追者曰：「吾既思戀而歸，理無反面。
units.literal: Han from afar told the pursuers: “I already long to return; in principle there is no turning back.
units.en: He shouted to them, “I mean to go home—I will not turn back.

units.zh: 吾之弓矢，汝曹足知，無為相逼，自取死也。
units.literal: My bow and arrows you lot fully know; do not press me and seek your own deaths.
units.en: You know my bow and arrows well enough—do not press me and bring death on yourselves.

units.literal: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
units.en: I have lived among you too long—I should have killed you.

units.zh: 汝可百步豎刀，吾射中者，汝便宜反；
units.literal: You can at a hundred paces set up a blade; if my shot hits, you then should turn back;
units.en: Plant a blade at a hundred paces—if I hit it, withdraw;

units.literal: if not center, you may come forward.”

units.zh: 歸騎解刀豎之，翰一發便中刀鐶，追騎乃散。
units.literal: Gui’s riders undid a blade and set it up; Han one shot then hit the blade ring; pursuing riders then scattered.
units.en: They fixed a blade; his first arrow struck the ring and they broke off the chase.

references.title: 晉書斠注 七十一v109–110
references.quote: 《晉書》校文五曰《御覽》七百四十四引前燕錄作誓不殺汝詳語意崔錄似得其眞又攷《通鑑》作恨恨不欲殺汝注恨恨相戀之情與誓字語意正合此語温公必有所本疑恨不殺汝四字卽恨恨不欲殺汝一語之譌脫
何事非君，何使非民；治亦進，亂亦進，伊尹也。

relatedSelectedSourceFields.before: I have dwelt in your state long; I regret not killing you.
relatedSelectedSourceFields.after: I have dwelt in your state a long time; I regret not killing you [the extant wording is probably corrupt (Jinshu Jiaozhu): the Tongjian reads “with lingering attachment I do not wish to kill you”; Yulan 744, quoting the Records of Former Yan, reads “I swear not to kill you”].
relatedSelectedSourceFields.sourceReason: Render the independently approved philological note entirely in English, preserving its judgment of textual corruption, both divergent readings, and all citations. The Chinese source remains unchanged and displayed separately. This is necessary because the production editorial replacement gate rejects Han characters even when the separate translation-field gate supports intentional philology.

relatedSelectedSourceFields.before: Although Yang Yu served Huang and grew daily closer, with favor and rank above the old retainers, his nature was humble, respectful, pure and frugal, firm, simple, kind and earnest; though he repeatedly held posts at the apex of the court, he was like a scholar in plain cloth.
relatedSelectedSourceFields.after: Although Yang Yu had served Murong Huang for only a short time, his favor and rank surpassed those of the old retainers. By nature he was humble, respectful, upright and frugal, firm and straightforward, compassionate and sincere; although he successively held leading posts at court, he lived like a scholar in plain clothes.
relatedSelectedSourceFields.sourceReason: 仕皝日近 means his service under Huang was recent or short, not that he grew daily closer to Huang. The complete unit retains the contrast in rank and his personal qualities.
